Package com.leap.leaplaughlove.reporting.recap

Record Class RecapPayload

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.leap.leaplaughlove.reporting.recap.RecapPayload
Record Components:
month - the month the recap covers
quiet - true when the client filled no orders in the month. Positions held from before still move, so a quiet recap can still carry a trading return, gainers and losers, a benchmark difference and a ranking; only the trading figures are empty
moneyMoved - how much the client traded
topTickers - up to five symbols by value traded, most first
topGainer - the symbol with the best return, or null when none gained
topGainers - up to five symbols that gained, best first
biggestLosers - up to five symbols that lost, worst first
tradingReturn - the month's trading return across every priced position
benchmark - the S&P 500's move over the month, or null when it has no prices
instrumentsTraded - how many different symbols the client traded
topSector - the sector the client traded most, or null when none of the symbols has one
topPercent - the smallest top slice of the month's clients, by trading return, the client is in; null until every client's recap is ranked, and when not in the top half
public record RecapPayload(YearMonth month, boolean quiet, RecapPayload.MoneyMoved moneyMoved, List<RecapPayload.TickerActivity> topTickers, RecapPayload.TopGainer topGainer, List<RecapPayload.SymbolReturn> topGainers, List<RecapPayload.SymbolReturn> biggestLosers, RecapPayload.TradingReturn tradingReturn, RecapPayload.Benchmark benchmark, int instrumentsTraded, RecapPayload.TopSector topSector, Integer topPercent) extends Record
One client's recap of one UTC month: everything the recap cards show, stored as JSON in reporting.client_recaps so opening a recap never recomputes it. Its shape is version 2; a change to it bumps that number.

Returns are trading returns: the gain on the positions the client held or traded in the month, valued at daily closes, over the most money each position had in it at once. Cash deposits and withdrawals play no part.
